title: Usage Insights docs & samples plan (route tagging + export reports)
author: Elliot Price
body:
## Purpose
This page defines the DevEx plan for documentation and minimal code samples required to successfully onboard customers to **Usage Insights (cost drivers by route/model)**.

Primary customer outcomes:
1) Customers can reliably **tag requests with a stable `route` identifier**.
2) Customers can interpret route/model cost and performance views in the Console.
3) Customers can **export** a bounded report (CSV + JSON) for FinOps / incident reviews.

This plan covers:
- Docs IA and page-level requirements
- SDK guidance (Python/TypeScript/Go) + REST header guidance
- Quickstart updates (minimal snippets)
- Troubleshooting + FAQ topics that reduce support load
- Acceptance criteria for GA docs readiness

---

## Audience
- **Engineering teams** instrumenting applications (primary)
- **ML/Platform teams** managing inference deployment and governance
- **FinOps / Ops** stakeholders pulling exports (secondary)

---

## Key decisions we must align to (docs MUST match)
Docs must reflect the canonical route definition and normalization rules from **ADR-0142**.

### Route definition (customer mental model)
`route` is a **customer-defined logical application endpoint** used for analytics attribution (not an HTTP path).

Good examples:
- `chat.completions`
- `support_rag`
- `agent.billing_dispute`
- `email-draft/v2`

Bad examples (likely to cause cardinality issues):
- `/users/12345/messages/987`
- `req_01J...`
- `user-<id>`
- `prompt:<hash>`

### Normalization + reserved values (docs must be explicit)
- Canonical routes are lowercased and restricted to ASCII with allowed chars: `a-z 0-9 . _ - /`.
- Max canonical length is **128**; longer values are rewritten to hashed form with `h/` prefix.
- Reserved buckets are platform-generated: `unknown`, `invalid`, `other`.
  - SDKs should prevent customers from intentionally setting these.

### Cardinality guidance (docs must warn)
Even syntactically valid routes can be rolled up to `other` when cardinality budgets are exceeded per org/project/env.

Docs must include explicit warnings against dynamic identifiers in the route.

---

## Docs information architecture (IA)
We will ship a small set of high-signal pages with clear cross-links.

### 1) Product overview page (Console + concepts)
**Proposed title:** "Usage Insights: cost drivers by route and model"

Must include:
- What Usage Insights is and what questions it answers
- What dimensions are available (route, model, environment, region, deployment mode)
- Data freshness expectations (near-real-time vs late metering; keep wording aligned with SLOs)
- A short "Getting started" checklist that links to Route Tagging + Export Reports

### 2) Route tagging guide (core DevEx page)
**Proposed title:** "Route tagging (recommended): attribute cost and latency to your app"

Must include:
- Definition of route + naming conventions
- How to set `route` using SDKs (Python/TS/Go)
- How to set `route` for raw REST calls (header guidance)
- Framework examples (1–2) that map common web routes → stable route labels
- Cardinality best practices + anti-patterns
- How to validate tagging coverage in Console (e.g., avoid `unknown` dominance)

### 3) Export reports guide
**Proposed title:** "Export Usage Insights reports (CSV/JSON)"

Must include:
- Where export lives in the Console (route list and route detail)
- What filters/time ranges are supported
- File formats and high-level schema description
- Limits (time range / rows / size) and what happens when exceeded
- Audit logging note (exports are audit logged; point to compliance description)
- How to use the exported report for common workflows:
  - weekly FinOps review
  - incident / cost review attachment
  - internal chargeback by route

### 4) Troubleshooting + FAQ
**Proposed title:** "Usage Insights troubleshooting"

Must include:
- "Why does my invoice not match route totals exactly?" (timing, late data, retention)
- "Why is `unknown` my top route?" (missing tagging; gateway fallback limitations)
- "Why do I see `h/...` routes?" (length hashing)
- "Why is everything rolled up to `other`?" (cardinality limits)
- "Why are some routes missing model breakdown?" (partial data during rollout/backfill windows)

---

## SDK guidance (minimum content to ship)
We will standardize the user-facing parameter name to **`route`** across SDKs, and map it to a single underlying request mechanism.

### Underlying wire format
- **Standard header:** `X-Redwood-Route: <route>`
- Header value is the *raw* route; server-side normalization is applied per ADR-0142.

Docs must state:
- Header is safe to set on every request.
- Route should be stable, low-cardinality, and human-meaningful.

### Python SDK (minimal snippet)
Doc snippet must show both non-streaming and streaming usage.

```python
from redwood import Redwood

client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"])

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
    route="support_rag",  # logical app endpoint
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the warranty policy."},
    ],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```

Streaming variant (ensure route is still set):
```python
with client.chat.completions.stream(
    model="redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
    route="chat.completions",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Draft a reply."}],
) as stream:
    for event in stream:
        if event.type == "message.delta":
            print(event.delta, end="")
```

### TypeScript SDK (minimal snippet)
```ts
import { Redwood } from "@redwood-inference/sdk";

const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY! });

const resp = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
  route: "email-draft/v2",
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Write a concise follow-up email." }],
});

console.log(resp.choices[0].message.content);
```

### Go SDK (minimal snippet)
```go
client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))

resp, err := client.ChatCompletions.Create(ctx, &redwood.ChatCompletionsRequest{
  Model: "redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
  Route: "agent.billing_dispute",
  Messages: []redwood.Message{{Role: "user", Content: "Explain the latest charge."}},
})
if err != nil { panic(err) }
fmt.Println(resp.Choices[0].Message.Content)
```

### Raw REST example (for unsupported environments)
```bash
curl https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Route: support_rag" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Help me troubleshoot my account."}]}'
```

---

## Naming conventions (include verbatim in docs)
### Recommended patterns
- Use dot- or underscore-separated logical names: `chat.completions`, `support_rag`.
- Use `/vN` suffix for versioning if needed: `email-draft/v2`.
- Keep route stable across environments; rely on the product’s environment dimension for splits.

### Avoid
- Any user/org identifiers (e.g., `user/123`, `org/acme`).
- Any request IDs, timestamps, UUIDs.
- Raw HTTP paths from app routers.

### Length and character rules (customer-friendly summary)
- Keep under 128 characters.
- Use lowercase ASCII.
- Allowed: `a-z 0-9 . _ - /`.

Docs should link to ADR-0142 for exact normalization behavior.

---

## Minimal examples required for GA
We will keep examples intentionally small and copy/pasteable.

### Required (GA)
1) One end-to-end request example per SDK (Python/TS/Go) with `route` set.
2) One REST `curl` example showing `X-Redwood-Route`.
3) One streaming example (Python or TS) demonstrating route tagging works with streams.
4) One framework mapping example:
   - Example: Express/FastAPI showing mapping from HTTP handler → a stable route label (e.g., `support_rag`).
5) One export workflow example:
   - Steps in Console to export a report for a time range and filters.

### Nice-to-have (post-GA)
- Terraform example for provisioning RBAC roles that allow exports.
- A “chargeback” example notebook that groups costs by route and outputs a summary.

---

## Export reports documentation requirements
Because export is frequently used by non-engineers, we must document it as an operational workflow.

Docs must clearly state:
- Export is a **bounded** report (size/time range limits apply).
- Exports respect org/project scoping and are **audit logged**.
- CSV is suitable for finance workflows; JSON is suitable for automation.

### CSV/JSON schema guidance (high-level)
We should describe fields at a conceptual level without freezing internal table names.

Minimum fields to describe:
- `time_window_start`, `time_window_end` (or a bucket timestamp)
- `route`
- `model` (and model variant, if applicable)
- cost fields: total cost, input tokens, output tokens, cached tokens (if available)
- performance fields: p50/p95 latency, error rate (if included in export scope)

Docs should include:
- A short note on cached tokens: “cached tokens may have different unit economics; use total cost for spend.”
- A note on late-arriving data: exports for the most recent window may shift slightly as metering finalizes.

---

## Console UX documentation hooks
To reduce confusion, the overview and route tagging pages should include:
- A screenshot or callout for where the `route` dimension appears in the UI.
- A callout when `unknown` is high: “You likely haven’t tagged routes yet.”
- A callout for `h/...`: “Route exceeded max length; it was hashed.”

(Engineering to provide staging screenshots; design to approve annotation style.)

---

## QA checklist (docs readiness)
Before publishing GA docs:
1) All snippets compile/run against staging.
2) Route normalization examples match ADR (casefolding, allowed chars, 128-char rule, reserved buckets).
3) Docs explicitly discourage dynamic identifiers and mention `other` rollup risk.
4) Export docs include limits and audit logging statement.
5) Troubleshooting covers top 5 support questions (`unknown`, mismatches, `h/`, `other`, missing breakdown).
6) Links from Console ("Learn more") land on the correct pages.
7) Accessibility: screenshots have alt text; tables are readable; headings are consistent.

---

## Open items / decisions needed from Eng + Product
1) Confirm final header name and whether we also expose a JSON field for route on raw REST requests.
2) Confirm whether exports include latency/error fields at GA (docs must match scope).
3) Confirm final export limits (max time range, max rows, max file size) to document.
4) Confirm whether gateway-derived fallback routes use `api/...` prefix (as per ADR) and how prominently we message that fallback is coarse.

---

## Appendix: Suggested copy for “Why route matters” (for overview page)
Adding a `route` to your inference requests lets Redwood attribute cost and performance to the parts of your product that trigger LLM usage. This enables teams to:
- Find the highest-spend application routes quickly
- Understand which models drive spend for each route
- Track week-over-week changes after releases
- Export a report for finance, chargeback, or incident reviews

If you don’t set a route, Redwood will attribute usage to `unknown` (or a coarse gateway-derived label), which limits the value of route-level insights.
